resources.string:
App Specifications and User Manual

Overview
Turbo Overlay Monitor is a lightweight on-screen monitoring tool designed for gaming and performance-focused sessions. It shows key device health information in a compact floating panel without using any internet API, cloud service, account login, or external server.

Privacy
This app is built for local device monitoring. It does not require an internet connection, does not upload data, and does not use any online API key. All displayed information is read locally from the device while the app is running.

Service Status
The status panel at the top shows whether the required local service is connected. When the service is unavailable, action buttons remain disabled. When the service is connected and permission is granted, supported controls become available.

Overlay Window
Tap Floating Overlay Window to start the floating monitor. Android may ask for Display over other apps permission. After permission is granted, a small transparent handle appears near the upper-left area of the screen.

Using the Overlay
Tap or swipe the handle to open the compact overlay panel. Use the Hide button inside the panel to close only the panel. The handle remains visible so the overlay can be opened again when needed.

Live Monitoring
The overlay shows CPU load and battery temperature with frequent refreshes. The graph keeps a short recent history so the app stays lightweight during games.

Graph Controls
Use the chip icon to view CPU load. Use the battery icon to view battery temperature. Use the performance icon to open performance controls. The selected option is highlighted.

Performance Controls
The performance controls are intended to request a smoother gaming state from the device. Support may vary by Android version, manufacturer, and system policy. If a command is not supported, the app continues running normally.

Performance Per Minute
The repeat performance option reapplies the performance request at a fixed interval while enabled. Use it only during gaming or testing, and turn it off when it is no longer needed.

Unavailable State
If the required service stops in the background, live values show N/A and protected controls are disabled until the service becomes available again.

Stop App
Stop App closes the overlay service and attempts to stop the app completely. Use it when you are done monitoring.
